text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, sends greeting to Moslems for Bairam, saying "these days in which we approach God will enlighten our efforts for a long-lasting peace and for the return of refugees".

- Deputy to international High Representative in Bosnia, Michael Steiner, demands Bosnian Serb authorities allow lawyers from Moslem-Croat federation to represent seven Moslem men who are due to be tried in Zvornik.
- United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Sadako Ogata, says that UNHCR will offer financial support for the reconstruction of 600 houses in the disputed Brcko area.

- Bosnian Serb Prime Minister Gojko Klickovic and Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic announce that the Serb republic and federation will start regulating goods transported across the inter-entity boundary line.

- The traditional, multi-ethnic and multi-cultural character of Bosnia is disappearing because of the recent genocidal campaign conducted against Bosnian Moslems, Enes Karic, a former minister for culture, says in a new book. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
